newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope invited to visit Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Pope invited to visit Taiwan.

text.p: Taiwan's Vice-President Lien Chan said he had invited Pope John Paul to visit the island during an audience on Tuesday and that the Roman Catholic leader had agreed to consider the offer.
"I invited His Holiness...to visit," Lien, the highest-ranking Taiwanese official to visit the Vatican, told a news conference. "He said he will consider our proposal," Lien said.
The Vatican is the only state in Europe which has diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which China regards as a rebel province.
China appeared irked by a statement by the Pope on Monday that the Vatican would closely watch how Catholics in Hong Kong were treated after the British colony is handed over to Beijing in July.

"We would hope to have no interference in our religious affairs, and when we talk about interference, the scope is very wide, not only including missionary work but also in appointments of bishops," a Chinese foreign ministry spokesman said.
